claims.claim_ar: الهمزة في «أَلَمْ» تعمل كأداة استفهام إنكاري توبيخي؛ أسلوب لحثّ على التذكير واللوم.
claims.claim_en: The hamza in 'أَلَمْ' functions as a negative rhetorical question (reproachful interrogation), a stylistic device for admonition and reminding.

claims.claim_ar: ذكر العقاب باسمه «نار جهنم» تعبير مقتضب وقوي يختزل المعنى ويؤكد شدة العاقبة (إيجاز وتكثيف دلالي).
claims.claim_en: Naming the punishment explicitly as 'the fire of Jahannam' is concise and forceful, compressing meaning and emphasizing the severity of the consequence (a form of concision/semantic compression).
claims.needs_review_reason: Interpretive assignment of 'ijaz'—the source chunk records the promise 'نار جهنم' but does not explicitly analyze it as 'إيجاز'; further textual/tafsir support recommended.
claims.rhetorical_effect: الإيحاء بالعقاب الحاسم لتحريض الخوف والردع (deterrent emphasis)

claims.claim_ar: صفة الخلود «خالِدًا» تؤكد ديمومة العقاب وعدم انتهاءه، ما يعزز وقع التهديد والتوبيخ.
claims.claim_en: The attribute of permanence 'khālid' (everlasting) underscores the permanence of the punishment, reinforcing the impact of the warning and reproach.
claims.needs_review_reason: Source chunk uses the plural form 'خالِدِينَ فِيها' while the ayah has singular 'خَالِدًا فِيهَا' — conceptual match likely but morphological alignment should be checked.
claims.rhetorical_effect: تكثيف الخوف من العقوبة عبر التأكيد على استمراريتها (heightened deterrence)

warnings: Provided source chunks are from Darwish (i'rab) and Safi; the developer request named authors (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, tafsir balagha) but those specific sources were not supplied. Claims therefore rely on the available chunks only.

Some source_quote_ar substrings used are not the exact word-forms in the ayah (e.g., source has plural 'خالِدِينَ فِيها' while the ayah uses singular 'خَالِدًا فِيهَا'). I noted such mismatches in needs_review_reason fields.

Interpretive classifications (e.g., labeling 'نار جهنم' as 'ijaz') are inferential and flagged as 'medium' confidence; further corroboration from rhetorical/tafsir sources is recommended for higher-certainty tagging.
